chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Dhubyān ibn Ḥakīm, from Mūsā ibn Ukayl al-Numayrī, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a restricted well into which a man fell and died, and it was not possible to bring him out of the well: may wudu (ablution) be performed from that well? He said: “Wudu (ablution) is not to be performed from it. It is to be abandoned and made a grave. And if it is possible to bring him out, he is to be brought out, washed, and buried.”
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “The sanctity of the Muslim man when dead is equal to his sanctity while he is alive.”

key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well, the site of the legal ruling in this report
key_terms.تُعَطَّلُ: it is to be abandoned and left unused
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: he is to be washed, referring to the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.قَبْرًا: a grave, meaning the well takes the ruling of a burial place if the body cannot be removed
key_terms.مَيِّتًا: while dead, indicating the deceased Muslim retains sacred inviolability
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: wudu (ablution) is performed, referring to ritual washing with the well water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using water from a well in which a dead body remains?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a well in which a person has died and cannot be recovered: its water is not to be used for wudu (ablution), and the well is to be left as his grave. If recovery is possible, the body should be removed, given ghusl, and buried, affirming the enduring sanctity of the deceased Muslim.
